status: G5 pilot: processed, compressed and reviewed; in the game beyond the west edge of Chapter VII's legion battle (desktop build, High)
use: Field artillery behind the Roman line, beyond the board's west edge, in the field battles of the larger commands.

generator.prompt: A Roman carroballista as shown on Trajan's Column: a bolt-shooting torsion engine mounted on a light two-wheeled cart, its two upright spring housings cased in bronze cylinders and joined by an arched iron bar, a long wooden slider with a winch at the back, on the plank bed of the cart with spoked wheels and a draught pole; a few spare bolts in a box on the bed. About two and a half metres long and one point eight metres high. Weathered wood, bronze and iron. Single isolated static prop for a grounded painterly-realistic historical game set in the third century Roman world. Physically based aged materials, believable hand-made construction and strong readable silhouette, restrained surface detail, level base and complete geometry from every side. No environment, ground plane, decorative display plinth, modern materials, text, logos or people.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the battles in the desktop build at High, before and after
review.notes: Two bronze-cased spring housings joined by an arched iron bar, as on Trajan's Column, with a slider running back along a plank bed, on a cart with four spoked wheels rather than the column's two. The springs stand at the model's -x, so it turns half round (yaw pi) to face east, toward the enemy. 3.3 m long with its pole; the byte budget rose from 280,000 to 290,000 for its 4,409 triangles. In the game, at the edge of the view behind the line, its thin frame and dark timber are hard to tell from the scrub; the onager reads better.
